caption: Performance of different triggers. The words used as triggers on the horizontal axis are arranged in ascending order according to the ASR of the clean model.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the Attack Success Rate (ASR) of different trigger words across three strategies—“start,” “random,” and “end”—for the AGNews dataset under dirty-label poisoning with 13 poisoned samples. The horizontal axis lists trigger words: “cf,” “bb,” “WNBA,” “ESPN,” “NHL,” “FIFA,” “Estadio,” and “athletics,” arranged in ascending order of the clean model’s ASR, as indicated in the caption. The vertical axis represents ASR, scaled linearly from 0.5 to 0.9 with tick marks at 0.1 intervals. The “start” strategy is depicted by a green line with circular markers, beginning at approximately 0.75 for “cf” and peaking at 0.9 for “WNBA,” then declining to about 0.85 for “athletics.” The “random” strategy is shown as an orange line with cross markers, starting at 0.5 for “cf,” rising to 0.8 at “WNBA,” dipping to 0.6 at “ESPN,” and ending at 0.78 for “athletics.” The “end” strategy is represented by a purple line with circular markers, starting at 0.6 for “cf,” rising sharply to 0.9 at “WNBA,” then decreasing to 0.8 at “ESPN,” rising again to 0.9 at “FIFA,” and finally settling at 0.82 for “athletics.”
